svg.text: HETEROGENEOUS SOC RESOURCE CONTENTION & POWER-RAIL INTERFERENCE
Shared Memory Crossbar Burst Starvation and Transient PDN Voltage Droop on Shared Silicon
SHARED SYSTEM CROSSBAR (AXI4/5 QoS) & 8MB LAST-LEVEL CACHE
⚡ Matrix tile burst evicts enforcer sensor tables from L3 (t_refill = 20ns → 350ns)
• Non-preemptive packet-atomic bursts (ARLEN ≤ 256 beats cannot be truncated)
Total Queuing Delay: t_wait = 20.0 + 5.0 + 2.5 + 0.1 (bank conflict) = 27.6 µs
DRAM Page Reordering: Arbiter favors open row locality, starving real-time closed-bank reads.
Result: Enforcer read latency explodes from nominal 5.0 µs to 27.6–80.0 µs under load.
ENFORCEMENT TIMING SLACK COLLAPSE (1.0 ms Control Cycle)
2. Contended Under NPU Burst: Total = 127.6 µs (Slack = -7.6 µs ✕)
DEADLINE BREACH: 7.6 µs Overrun into Valve Transit Margin
Although average channel utilization is only 25%, instantaneous burst collisions
exhaust timing margins and delay high-pressure shutoff command.
(b) PDN Transient Voltage Droop & Clock Jitter
CH2: Supply Voltage V_core(t) on Shared Rail
CH3: RT Core Propagation Delay & Clock Jitter
• VRM loop bandwidth (<1 MHz) is 3 orders of magnitude too slow for nanosecond di/dt steps.
• Logic propagation delay t_prop proportional to V_DD/(V_DD-V_th)^2 causes setup-time violations.
• DVFS emergency throttle cuts clock to 600 MHz: t_exec = 0.70ms → 1.40ms > 1.0ms deadline.
Verdict: Software isolation is defeated by power grid impedance and thermal substrate coupling.
